prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title: 'Asthma medicines: two different jobs'. Two horizontal lanes constructed from beautifully painted OBJECTS and paths, without prose boxes or biological anatomy. Top lane: a simple unbranded inhaler icon labelled 'Salbutamol' beside a stopwatch, followed by a SHORT teal path to an opening abstract coiled spring loop. Large lane heading 'RELIEVER'. Small labels 'Minutes' and 'Relaxes smooth muscle'. The spring is explicitly a mechanical metaphor, not an airway. Bottom lane: a DIFFERENT unbranded inhaler icon labelled 'Inhaled corticosteroid', then a LONG path alongside a paper calendar with repeated daily checkmarks, leading to a broad teal protective shield with a small coral inflammation-flame symbol becoming fainter beside it. Large heading 'PREVENTER'. Short labels 'Regular use' and 'Controls inflammation over time'. No curves with invented measurements, no numerical dose, no anatomy, no lungs, no comparisons of actual inhaler colours. Footer line 'Follow the prescribed asthma plan'. Plenty of white space; paths have clear arrowheads.

clinicalSources.title: NHLBI — Asthma treatment and action plan

teaching.question: Why does a child's prescribed inhaled corticosteroid need regular use even when salbutamol relieves symptoms quickly?
teaching.answer: Salbutamol rapidly relaxes airway smooth muscle. Inhaled corticosteroid controls the underlying inflammation over time, helping reduce future symptoms and attacks.

title: Reliever and preventer have different jobs
caption: Salbutamol gives rapid relief by relaxing airway smooth muscle. Regular inhaled corticosteroid controls inflammation over time and reduces future symptoms and attacks.
alt: A short stopwatch path illustrates rapid salbutamol relief, while a longer calendar path illustrates ongoing inhaled-corticosteroid control.
